FIB_PLUS	<p>36f4_8978</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1c6e49;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1c6e49;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c6e49;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1a6299;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1a6299;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1a6299;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377c;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8f377c;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f377c;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cpy, +++, cpy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c05;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #715c05;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c05;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196c61;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #196c61;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196c61;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377c;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8f377c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f377c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jrw, +++, jrw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>8bc2_e87f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8b4a21;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c6e49;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1c6e49;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c6e49;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bfh, +++, bfh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>487b_51e3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #196c61;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #196c61;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196c61;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963956;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #963956;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #963956;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fkr, +++, fkr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>8a01_91cc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c05;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #715c05;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c05;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #136a72;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #136a72;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #136a72;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377c;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8f377c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8b4a21;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006885;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f36a6;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7f36a6;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5c6419;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #5c6419;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5c6419;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963956;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #963956;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #963956;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, btw, +++, btw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>3db5_51ba</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5c6419;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #5c6419;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5c6419;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006885;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377c;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8f377c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>4c44_219a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196c61;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #196c61;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196c61;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8b4a21;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3a6c24;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f36a6;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7f36a6;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>62de_aed1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8b4a21;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196c61;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #196c61;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196c61;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cem, +++, cem"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b4a21;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3a6c24;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1a6299;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1a6299;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>196e_b228</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b4a21;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3a6c24;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006885;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, erx, +++, erx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03328;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a03328;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03328;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3a6c24;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ptx, +++, ptx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. FIB_PLUS	<p>f296_3ec3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b4a21;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a21;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196c61;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #196c61;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196c61;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>5d63_5ff9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c05;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #715c05;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c05;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006885;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377c;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8f377c;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>09c4_ffd0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c05;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #715c05;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c05;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196c61;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #196c61;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196c61;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377c;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8f377c;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1a6299;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1a6299;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1a6299;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377c;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8f377c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". FIB_PLUS	<p>9bed_02a4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03328;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a03328;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03328;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3a6c24;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a6c24;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bkm, +++, bkm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03328;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a03328;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03328;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c6e49;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1c6e49;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c6e49;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jtw, +++, jtw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c05;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #715c05;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c05;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1a6299;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1a6299;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1a6299;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963956;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #963956;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03328;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a03328;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03328;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196c61;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #196c61;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196c61;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3957b1;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3957b1;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, djk, +++, djk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
